source.primary_manuscript: Codex Vaticanus (B/03; Vatican Library Gr. 1209, 4th c. CE ~325-350)
source.primary_manuscript_contains: Essentially complete New Testament; in Mark, Vaticanus ENDS at 16:8 (followed by a blank column — a paleographically significant scribal feature absent elsewhere in the codex, taken by Metzger and Aland as evidence the scribe knew of a longer ending but did not transmit it).
source.secondary_manuscript: Codex Sinaiticus (א/01; British Library Add. 43725 + Sinai + Leipzig + St. Petersburg fragments, 4th c. CE ~330-360) — also ends Mark at 16:8.
source.early_papyri_cross_collation: No early-papyrus witness preserves Mark 16:9-20. The earliest witnesses TO 16:9-20 are 5th c. (Codex Alexandrinus A/02, Codex Bezae D/05, Codex Ephraemi Rescriptus C/04, Codex Washingtonianus W/032). Vaticanus + Sinaiticus + Codex Bobiensis (k; 4th-5th c. Old Latin) + Sinaitic Syriac + some Armenian + some Georgian mss END at 16:8. The Sahidic + Bohairic Coptic traditions split.
source.reference_critical_apparatus: NA28 (Nestle-Aland 28th, 2012); UBS5 (United Bible Societies 5th, 2014); SBLGNT (SBL 2010); THGNT (Tyndale House 2017). All modern critical editions print 16:9-20 in double-brackets [[ ]] indicating dubious authenticity; THGNT relegates the longer ending to an apparatus / appendix.
source.transliteration_convention: Scholarly Koine Greek transliteration (SBL convention): polytonic-stripped lowercase Latin with diacritics for breathings (h- for rough; nothing for smooth) and Greek-specific letters (ē for eta, ō for omega, ph for phi, ch for chi, ps for psi, th for theta, rh for rho with rough breathing); ai/ei/oi/au/eu/ou diphthongs preserved; accent marks generally omitted in scholarly translit
source.verificationStatus: best-effort reconstruction; verification pending against Vaticanus + Sinaiticus + Alexandrinus + Bezae + Washingtonianus original codicology + the NA28/UBS5/SBLGNT critical apparatus
source.fetchedFrom: SBLGNT public-domain edition (Holmes 2010) + NA28 reference + Metzger UBS Textual Commentary on the GNT (2nd ed. 1994) ad loc.
source.citation: Aland, Aland, Karavidopoulos, Martini, Metzger, eds., *Novum Testamentum Graece*, 28th ed. (Nestle-Aland, Stuttgart 2012). UBS5 = Aland et al., *The Greek New Testament*, 5th ed. (United Bible Societies 2014). Holmes, M. W., ed., *The Greek New Testament: SBL Edition* (SBL 2010; public-domain). Jongkind, D., ed., *The Greek New Testament*, Tyndale House (Crossway 2017). Metzger, B. M., *A Textual Commentary on the Greek New Testament*, 2nd ed. (UBS 1994) 102-106. Aland, K. & Aland, B., *The Text of the New Testament*, 2nd ed. (Eerdmans 1989). Codex Vaticanus: Vatican Library Gr. 1209 (4th c.). Codex Sinaiticus: British Library Add. 43725 + Sinai + Leipzig + St. Petersburg (4th c.). Codex Alexandrinus: British Library Royal 1 D. V-VIII (5th c.). Codex Bezae: Cambridge UL Nn.II.41 (5th c.). Codex Washingtonianus: Smithsonian Freer Gallery Cod. W 06.274 (4th-5th c.). Codex Bobiensis: Turin G.VII.15 (4th-5th c. Old Latin k). France NIGTC 2002; Marcus AB 2009; Collins Hermeneia 2007; Hooker BNTC 1991; Croy *The Mutilation of Mark's Gospel* (Abingdon 2003); Kelhoffer *Miracle and Mission* (Mohr Siebeck 2000) — definitive study of the longer ending.
source.paleography_note: The Koine Greek text is preserved in polytonic form as transmitted via SBLGNT. THE PRIMARY TEXTUAL-CRITICAL DISPUTE OF MARK 16: verses 1-8 are the secure original ending; verses 9-20 (the 'Longer Ending of Mark') are absent in Vaticanus + Sinaiticus + Bobiensis + Sinaitic Syriac and are universally regarded by modern textual critics (Metzger, Aland-Aland, Ehrman, Marcus, Collins, Croy, Kelhoffer) as a 2nd-century scribal addition composed to harmonize Mark's truncated ending with the resurrection-appearance narratives of Matthew, Luke, and John. A separate 'Shorter Ending' (a single sentence between v.8 and v.9 in some witnesses including L, Ψ, 099, 0112) and a 'Freer Logion' (an additional expansion between v.14 and v.15 unique to Codex Washingtonianus) are documented but not reproduced in this source file. All 20 verses are preserved here per WoH-Translation textual-critical convention to enable full-chapter downstream translation; verses 9-20 are flagged at each verse as part of the longer ending. The early Greek manuscripts use scriptio continua. Nomina sacra appear abbreviated in the uncials.

verses.text: Καὶ διαγενομένου τοῦ σαββάτου Μαρία ἡ Μαγδαληνὴ καὶ Μαρία ἡ τοῦ Ἰακώβου καὶ Σαλώμη ἠγόρασαν ἀρώματα ἵνα ἐλθοῦσαι ἀλείψωσιν αὐτόν.
verses.translit: Kai diagenomenou tou sabbatou Maria hē Magdalēnē kai Maria hē tou Iakōbou kai Salōmē ēgorasan arōmata hina elthousai aleipsōsin auton.
verses.notes: EMPTY-TOMB OPENING. Three women named: Mary Magdalene, Mary (mother) of James, and Salome. The shopping-for-spices detail implies the visit is post-Sabbath (Saturday evening or pre-dawn Sunday). *aleipsōsin* = anoint (oil/ointment), distinct from John's *enetaphiasen* (full burial-preparation). Marcus AB 1079-1080; France NIGTC 676-678.

verses.text: καὶ λίαν πρωῒ τῇ μιᾷ τῶν σαββάτων ἔρχονται ἐπὶ τὸ μνημεῖον ἀνατείλαντος τοῦ ἡλίου.
verses.translit: kai lian prōi tē mia tōn sabbatōn erchontai epi to mnēmeion anateilantos tou hēliou.
verses.notes: *lian prōi* (very early) + *anateilantos tou hēliou* (sun having risen) is a famous internal-tension Markan dating phrase — the women set out before dawn but arrive after sunrise. *tē mia tōn sabbatōn* = literally 'the first (day) of the week' (Sunday).

verses.text: καὶ ἔλεγον πρὸς ἑαυτάς· Τίς ἀποκυλίσει ἡμῖν τὸν λίθον ἐκ τῆς θύρας τοῦ μνημείου;
verses.translit: kai elegon pros heautas· Tis apokylisei hēmin ton lithon ek tēs thyras tou mnēmeiou?
verses.notes: The rolling-stone seal of the rock-cut tomb (cf. 15:46). *apokylisei* = will roll away. The women's practical concern frames the discovery.

verses.text: καὶ ἀναβλέψασαι θεωροῦσιν ὅτι ἀποκεκύλισται ὁ λίθος, ἦν γὰρ μέγας σφόδρα.
verses.translit: kai anablepsasai theōrousin hoti apokekylistai ho lithos, ēn gar megas sphodra.
verses.notes: *megas sphodra* = exceedingly great. Mark's parenthetical emphasis on stone-size heightens the prodigy.

verses.text: καὶ εἰσελθοῦσαι εἰς τὸ μνημεῖον εἶδον νεανίσκον καθήμενον ἐν τοῖς δεξιοῖς περιβεβλημένον στολὴν λευκήν, καὶ ἐξεθαμβήθησαν.
verses.translit: kai eiselthousai eis to mnēmeion eidon neaniskon kathēmenon en tois dexiois peribeblēmenon stolēn leukēn, kai exethambēthēsan.
verses.notes: MAJOR THEME — the *neaniskos* (young man) in white. Mark does NOT call him an angel (contrast Matt 28:2 *angelos kyriou*; Luke 24:4 *andres dyo en esthēti astraptousē*). The cross-corpus echo of the *neaniskos* in 14:51-52 (the naked fleeing young man at the arrest) is a famous Markan literary puzzle. **LENS-RISK FLAG**: do not pre-resolve toward (a) angelic interpretation or (b) Raëlian extraterrestrial-messenger reading; preserve the surface ambiguity that Mark deliberately leaves open. Marcus AB 1080-1081; Collins Hermeneia 794-795.

verses.text: ὁ δὲ λέγει αὐταῖς· Μὴ ἐκθαμβεῖσθε· Ἰησοῦν ζητεῖτε τὸν Ναζαρηνὸν τὸν ἐσταυρωμένον· ἠγέρθη, οὐκ ἔστιν ὧδε· ἴδε ὁ τόπος ὅπου ἔθηκαν αὐτόν·
verses.translit: ho de legei autais· Mē ekthambeisthe· Iēsoun zēteite ton Nazarēnon ton estaurōmenon· ēgerthē, ouk estin hōde· ide ho topos hopou ethēkan auton·
verses.notes: **MAJOR RESURRECTION-ANNOUNCEMENT VERSE**. *ēgerthē* = aorist passive 'he was raised' (the standard NT theological-passive for the resurrection-event). The combination *Nazarēnon ton estaurōmenon* (the Nazarene the crucified one) is a deliberately stark identification. **LENS-RISK FLAG**: do not pre-resolve toward the Raëlian-canon reading of the resurrection (Raël *The Book Which Tells the Truth* reads the resurrection as a cloning-event); preserve the announcement-surface.

verses.text: ἀλλὰ ὑπάγετε εἴπατε τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ καὶ τῷ Πέτρῳ ὅτι Προάγει ὑμᾶς εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν· ἐκεῖ αὐτὸν ὄψεσθε, καθὼς εἶπεν ὑμῖν.
verses.translit: alla hypagete eipate tois mathētais autou kai tō Petrō hoti Proagei hymas eis tēn Galilaian· ekei auton opsesthe, kathōs eipen hymin.
verses.notes: Galilee-promise (cross-corpus 14:28). The singling-out of Peter (*kai tō Petrō*) after his denial (14:66-72) is a Markan rehabilitation hint. NO resurrection-appearance is narrated in Mark; only the promise. This is the load-bearing detail for the 16:8 ending theory.

verses.text: καὶ ἐξελθοῦσαι ἔφυγον ἀπὸ τοῦ μνημείου, εἶχεν γὰρ αὐτὰς τρόμος καὶ ἔκστασις· καὶ οὐδενὶ οὐδὲν εἶπαν, ἐφοβοῦντο γάρ.
verses.translit: kai exelthousai ephygon apo tou mnēmeiou, eichen gar autas tromos kai ekstasis· kai oudeni ouden eipan, ephobounto gar.
verses.notes: **THE ORIGINAL ENDING OF MARK** (per Vaticanus + Sinaiticus + Bobiensis + Sinaitic Syriac + consensus modern critical view). The Gospel ends mid-sentence on the conjunction *gar* ("for") — *ephobounto gar* = 'for they were afraid.' This is one of the most-discussed endings in world literature: a Gospel that announces resurrection but narrates fear, silence, and flight. Scholarship debates whether (a) Mark deliberately ended this way (Magness 1986; Marcus 2009; Lincoln 1989), (b) the original ending was lost and recovered/replaced in transmission (Croy 2003), or (c) Mark's autograph was unfinished (Hooker 1991). The longer ending (vv.9-20) is the 2nd-century scribal solution to the perceived problem. Marcus AB 1088-1096; Collins Hermeneia 797-801; France NIGTC 670-674.

verses.text: Ἀναστὰς δὲ πρωῒ πρώτῃ σαββάτου ἐφάνη πρῶτον Μαρίᾳ τῇ Μαγδαληνῇ, παρ’ ἧς ἐκβεβλήκει ἑπτὰ δαιμόνια.
verses.translit: Anastas de prōi prōtē sabbatou ephanē prōton Maria tē Magdalēnē, par’ hēs ekbeblēkei hepta daimonia.
verses.notes: **LONGER-ENDING VERSE — ABSENT IN VATICANUS + SINAITICUS + BOBIENSIS + SINAITIC SYRIAC**; consensus modern critical view (Metzger UBS Textual Commentary 102-106; Aland-Aland 1989; Marcus AB 2009; Collins Hermeneia 2007) is that 16:9-20 is a 2nd-century scribal addition composed to harmonize Mark with the resurrection-appearance narratives of the other Gospels. Preserved here per WoH-Translation textual-critical convention; the dispute is documented in this apparatus. INTERNAL EVIDENCE OF SECONDARY COMPOSITION: the vocabulary and style of vv.9-20 diverge sharply from Mark 1-16:8 (the longer ending contains 18 hapax legomena and uses 5 words found nowhere else in Mark); the narrative awkwardly reintroduces Mary Magdalene (already named in v.1) as if for the first time. **CONTENT**: first resurrection-appearance to Mary Magdalene (paralleling John 20:11-18). The 'seven demons' detail parallels Luke 8:2. **LENS-RISK FLAG**: do not pre-resolve toward Raëlian readings of the resurrection-appearances.

verses.text: ἐκείνη πορευθεῖσα ἀπήγγειλεν τοῖς μετ’ αὐτοῦ γενομένοις πενθοῦσι καὶ κλαίουσιν·
verses.translit: ekeinē poreutheisa apēngeilen tois met’ autou genomenois penthousi kai klaiousin·
verses.notes: **LONGER-ENDING VERSE — ABSENT IN VATICANUS + SINAITICUS + BOBIENSIS + SINAITIC SYRIAC**; 2nd-c. scribal addition per consensus (Metzger; Aland-Aland; Marcus; Collins). The phrase *tois met’ autou genomenois* (those who had been with him) is a uniquely circumlocutory designation for the disciples, not found in Mark 1-16:8 — internal stylistic evidence of secondary composition.

verses.text: κἀκεῖνοι ἀκούσαντες ὅτι ζῇ καὶ ἐθεάθη ὑπ’ αὐτῆς ἠπίστησαν.
verses.translit: kakeinoi akousantes hoti zē kai etheathē hyp’ autēs ēpistēsan.
verses.notes: **LONGER-ENDING VERSE — ABSENT IN VATICANUS + SINAITICUS + BOBIENSIS + SINAITIC SYRIAC**; 2nd-c. scribal addition per consensus. The disciples' disbelief of Mary Magdalene parallels Luke 24:11.

verses.text: Μετὰ δὲ ταῦτα δυσὶν ἐξ αὐτῶν περιπατοῦσιν ἐφανερώθη ἐν ἑτέρᾳ μορφῇ πορευομένοις εἰς ἀγρόν·
verses.translit: Meta de tauta dysin ex autōn peripatousin ephanerōthē en hetera morphē poreuomenois eis agron·
verses.notes: **LONGER-ENDING VERSE — ABSENT IN VATICANUS + SINAITICUS + BOBIENSIS + SINAITIC SYRIAC**; 2nd-c. scribal addition per consensus. Compressed allusion to the Luke 24:13-35 Emmaus-road appearance. *en hetera morphē* (in another form) is striking and unique. **LENS-RISK FLAG**: do not pre-resolve toward (a) docetic/transformation readings or (b) Raëlian shape-changing readings; preserve the phrase's ambiguity.

verses.text: κἀκεῖνοι ἀπελθόντες ἀπήγγειλαν τοῖς λοιποῖς· οὐδὲ ἐκείνοις ἐπίστευσαν.
verses.translit: kakeinoi apelthontes apēngeilan tois loipois· oude ekeinois episteusan.
verses.notes: **LONGER-ENDING VERSE — ABSENT IN VATICANUS + SINAITICUS + BOBIENSIS + SINAITIC SYRIAC**; 2nd-c. scribal addition per consensus. Repeated-disbelief motif (echoing v.11).

verses.text: Ὕστερον δὲ ἀνακειμένοις αὐτοῖς τοῖς ἕνδεκα ἐφανερώθη, καὶ ὠνείδισεν τὴν ἀπιστίαν αὐτῶν καὶ σκληροκαρδίαν ὅτι τοῖς θεασαμένοις αὐτὸν ἐγηγερμένον οὐκ ἐπίστευσαν.
verses.translit: Hysteron de anakeimenois autois tois hendeka ephanerōthē, kai ōneidisen tēn apistian autōn kai sklērokardian hoti tois theasamenois auton egēgermenon ouk episteusan.
verses.notes: **LONGER-ENDING VERSE — ABSENT IN VATICANUS + SINAITICUS + BOBIENSIS + SINAITIC SYRIAC**; 2nd-c. scribal addition per consensus. The 'eleven' (without Judas) at table. **TEXTUAL NOTE — THE FREER LOGION**: Codex Washingtonianus (W/032; 4th-5th c.) preserves a UNIQUE expansion inserted between v.14 and v.15 (the so-called 'Freer Logion'), in which the disciples defend themselves and Jesus speaks of Satan's power being ended. Jerome reports knowing this expansion (Contra Pelagium 2.15). The Freer Logion is documented in the apparatus but NOT reproduced in the standard SBLGNT/NA28 text — it is treated as an additional later scribal expansion beyond the longer ending itself.

verses.text: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Πορευθέντες εἰς τὸν κόσμον ἅπαντα κηρύξατε τὸ εὐαγγέλιον πάσῃ τῇ κτίσει.
verses.translit: kai eipen autois· Poreuthentes eis ton kosmon hapanta kēryxate to euangelion pasē tē ktisei.
verses.notes: **LONGER-ENDING VERSE — ABSENT IN VATICANUS + SINAITICUS + BOBIENSIS + SINAITIC SYRIAC**; 2nd-c. scribal addition per consensus. The 'Great Commission' analogue (paralleling Matt 28:18-20). *pasē tē ktisei* (to all creation) is a striking universalizing phrase. **LENS-RISK FLAG**: do not pre-resolve toward cosmic-mission / panspermia readings; preserve.

verses.text: ὁ πιστεύσας καὶ βαπτισθεὶς σωθήσεται, ὁ δὲ ἀπιστήσας κατακριθήσεται.
verses.translit: ho pisteusas kai baptistheis sōthēsetai, ho de apistēsas katakrithēsetai.
verses.notes: **LONGER-ENDING VERSE — ABSENT IN VATICANUS + SINAITICUS + BOBIENSIS + SINAITIC SYRIAC**; 2nd-c. scribal addition per consensus. Baptism-and-faith soteriology — a notably developed formula reflecting 2nd-century church-practice rather than 1st-century Markan theology (internal evidence of secondary composition; Kelhoffer 2000).

verses.text: σημεῖα δὲ τοῖς πιστεύσασιν ταῦτα παρακολουθήσει· ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί μου δαιμόνια ἐκβαλοῦσιν, γλώσσαις λαλήσουσιν καιναῖς,
verses.translit: sēmeia de tois pisteusasin tauta parakolouthēsei· en tō onomati mou daimonia ekbalousin, glōssais lalēsousin kainais,
verses.notes: **LONGER-ENDING VERSE — ABSENT IN VATICANUS + SINAITICUS + BOBIENSIS + SINAITIC SYRIAC**; 2nd-c. scribal addition per consensus. The five accompanying-signs catalogue begins here: (1) exorcism; (2) new tongues. Cross-corpus to Acts 2:4 (Pentecost glossolalia).

verses.text: καὶ ἐν ταῖς χερσὶν ὄφεις ἀροῦσιν, κἂν θανάσιμόν τι πίωσιν οὐ μὴ αὐτοὺς βλάψῃ, ἐπὶ ἀρρώστους χεῖρας ἐπιθήσουσιν καὶ καλῶς ἕξουσιν.
verses.translit: kai en tais chersin opheis arousin, kan thanasimon ti piōsin ou mē autous blapsē, epi arrōstous cheiras epithēsousin kai kalōs hexousin.
verses.notes: **LONGER-ENDING VERSE — ABSENT IN VATICANUS + SINAITICUS + BOBIENSIS + SINAITIC SYRIAC**; 2nd-c. scribal addition per consensus. **RAËLIAN CANON CITATION SITE**: this verse (the snake-handling / poison-immunity / laying-on-of-hands sayings) is engaged in *Extraterrestrials Took Me To Their Planet* (Raël 1975). Flag for Editor; acknowledgment-without-endorsement framework applies. The signs-catalogue continues: (3) serpent-handling; (4) poison-immunity; (5) healing. Cross-corpus to Acts 28:3-6 (Paul on Malta). This verse is the textual basis for the small Appalachian serpent-handling tradition (Burton *Serpent-Handling Believers* 1993). Kelhoffer 2000 surveys the patristic reception. **LENS-RISK FLAG**: do not pre-resolve.

verses.text: Ὁ μὲν οὖν κύριος Ἰησοῦς μετὰ τὸ λαλῆσαι αὐτοῖς ἀνελήμφθη εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ ἐκάθισεν ἐκ δεξιῶν τοῦ θεοῦ.
verses.translit: Ho men oun kyrios Iēsous meta to lalēsai autois anelēmphthē eis ton ouranon kai ekathisen ek dexiōn tou theou.
verses.notes: **LONGER-ENDING VERSE — ABSENT IN VATICANUS + SINAITICUS + BOBIENSIS + SINAITIC SYRIAC**; 2nd-c. scribal addition per consensus. **THE MARKAN ASCENSION VERSE**. **MAJOR RAËLIAN CANON CITATION SITE**: this verse (the Ascension) is engaged in *Extraterrestrials Took Me To Their Planet* (Raël 1975) — the Ascension is read as the Elohim's departure-by-craft. Acknowledgment-without-endorsement framework MUST be applied at the Editor stage. Flag for Editor. **PHILOLOGICALLY**: *anelēmphthē* = aorist passive 'was taken up' (theological-passive). Cross-corpus to Luke 24:51 + Acts 1:9-11 (the canonical Ascension narrative). *ek dexiōn tou theou* (at the right hand of God) — cross-corpus Ps 110:1 (109:1 LXX), citing Mark 12:36 + 14:62. **LENS-RISK FLAG**: preserve the ascension-surface; do not pre-resolve toward (a) the conventional theological reading or (b) the Raëlian craft-departure reading.

verses.text: ἐκεῖνοι δὲ ἐξελθόντες ἐκήρυξαν πανταχοῦ, τοῦ κυρίου συνεργοῦντος καὶ τὸν λόγον βεβαιοῦντος διὰ τῶν ἐπακολουθούντων σημείων.
verses.translit: ekeinoi de exelthontes ekēryxan pantachou, tou kyriou synergountos kai ton logon bebaiountos dia tōn epakolouthountōn sēmeiōn.
verses.notes: **LONGER-ENDING CLOSING VERSE — ABSENT IN VATICANUS + SINAITICUS + BOBIENSIS + SINAITIC SYRIAC**; 2nd-c. scribal addition per consensus (Metzger UBS Textual Commentary 102-106; Aland-Aland 1989; Marcus AB 2009; Collins Hermeneia 2007). The mission-fulfillment summary functions as a narratively-satisfying replacement for the abrupt v.8 ending — the very kind of closure that the consensus identifies as the scribal motive for composing the longer ending. **TEXTUAL NOTE — THE SHORTER ENDING**: a separate 'Shorter Ending' (a single sentence describing the women reporting briefly to Peter's circle and then Jesus himself sending out the proclamation of eternal salvation through them) is preserved in L, Ψ, 099, 0112, 274mg, 579, and some Sahidic + Bohairic Coptic + Ethiopic witnesses, sometimes appearing BETWEEN v.8 and v.9, sometimes INSTEAD of vv.9-20. The Shorter Ending is documented but not reproduced in this source file. **LENS-RISK FLAG**: chapter-end.
